A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REALM, with readable main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary materials. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original depth, segmentation and feature-matching experiments, alongside representation ablations, masking visualizations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative ablations, extended depth comparisons, reconstruction examples and cross-dataset evaluations.

M1.justification: V3 adds a 5M-parameter convolutional image-reconstruction head in S6.1. The core DUNE alignment encoder, LoRA adaptation, dual masking and losses remain unchanged. Existing head specifications are also revised, but the changed segmentation input width alongside unchanged parameter counts does not establish an actual architecture replacement.

E1.justification: V3 adds image reconstruction on VECtor and M3ED using a head trained on NYUv2. M3ED, previously used for distillation, also becomes an evaluation dataset for depth and segmentation under cross-dataset head transfer (S6). These extend task and domain coverage beyond the retained original benchmarks.

E2.justification: New Table 2 substantially extends the depth comparison with EReFormer, Depth AnyEvent and Depth Any Event Stream. These methods did not participate in v1's comparisons. The original depth, segmentation and matching comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces extended depth metrics and efficiency comparisons, LoRA rank/module controls, a masking control and cross-dataset head-transfer protocols. The main-text learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 1e-3 and depth-head training from 100 to 300 epochs, matching settings already stated in v1's appendix rather than establishing reruns. The stated depth-bin interval changes from 1–81 m to 1.95–82 m. The new segmentation transfer protocol remains ambiguous: S6.2 names NYUv2 training, while Figure S5 names DSEC.

E4.justification: Tables S1–S2 add LoRA rank and attention-versus-feed-forward ablations and a quantitative masked-versus-unmasked comparison at rank 16. The latter supplements v1's qualitative masking analysis with downstream depth and segmentation measurements. S6 also adds cross-dataset generalization analysis; the earlier representation ablation and wide-viewpoint analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Table S9 reports 1000 timing runs and mean times with ± values for the backbone and task heads. This is a separate experiment, not an increase to the retained 50-iteration matching benchmark. Neither version reports training-seed uncertainty or significance tests for the accuracy comparisons.

E6.justification: The original benchmark scores and corresponding appendix results are retained; VECtor AUC fractions are simply converted to percentages. V3 adds extended depth and efficiency results, ablation outcomes, reconstruction examples and M3ED results. For example, Table S2 reports masked versus unmasked mIoU of 55.47 versus 53.97 and depth RMSE of 8.06 versus 8.42. Table S10 newly reports M3ED mIoU of 26.95 for REALM versus 24.08 for DUNE. These are additional comparisons, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The LoRA formulation, spatial dilation curriculum and loss equations retain their mathematical substance. Equation 1 makes summation limits and mask indexing/time dependence explicit, without introducing a different derivation or formal result. Neither version provides theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central scientific claims: a shared RGB–event manifold, lightweight LoRA alignment, transfer of RGB-trained heads and state-of-the-art event feature matching. The additional experiments support these retained contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: V3 moderates the depth discussion from surpassing specialized architectures to competitive accuracy with lower decoder cost. It expands the existing resolution and temporal limitations by identifying tiling and memory holding as workarounds. It also states potential applicability beyond DUNE and interprets the new reconstruction and transfer results as broader latent-space generalization.

D1.justification: V3 adds reconstruction-head size and training-data quantity, hardware annotations for depth timing, and runtime settings. It consistently states code/model availability, replacing v1's mixed release-upon-acceptance wording while retaining the existing project address. S5.2 revises segmentation input width from 1024 to 768, although Table S8 retains 11,275 head parameters, leaving that specification unresolved. Most detailed training and preprocessing instructions were already present in v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds the three recent depth-method references, NYUv2 and MegaDepth, and sharpens its positioning relative to distillation between other sensor modalities. The overall related-work organization and claimed relationship to DUNE remain stable. Reference deduplication and publication-detail updates do not constitute additional substantive changes.

P1.justification: V3 makes targeted prose edits, defines zero-shot explicitly, separates limitations from the conclusion, and adds appendix subsections for the new analyses. It also updates author/publication text and standardizes terminology and references. The main narrative and most existing paragraphs retain their structure.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the displayed evidence with an extended depth comparison, LoRA and masking tables, backbone/head timing and domain-transfer tables, plus reconstruction and M3ED segmentation panels. Existing figures and tables are largely retained with relocation and caption edits. The VECtor comparison is reformatted to display AUC percentages rather than fractions.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens support for its design choices through quantitative masking and LoRA ablations, updates depth comparisons, and presents a more measured accuracy–efficiency interpretation. It also reconciles the main-text learning rate and training duration with existing appendix details. These are clear benefits, but ambiguous training provenance in S6.2/Figure S5, the segmentation-width inconsistency and mixed-hardware latency comparisons limit the strength and reproducibility of the added evidence.
